For a patient with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), **primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)** is preferred over fibrinolysis (clot-busting drugs) if it can be performed within **90 minutes of first medical contact** [ACC/AHA Acute Coronary Syndrome Guideline, 2025]. This is the standard of care for STEMI when PCI resources are available promptly. 

If PCI is not available within this timeframe, fibrinolysis may be considered as an alternative [ACC/AHA Acute Coronary Syndrome Guideline, 2025]. Additionally, **dual antiplatelet therapy** (aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor) is recommended regardless of the reperfusion strategy [ACC/AHA Acute Coronary Syndrome Guideline, 2025]. 

Always confirm local capabilities and adhere to regional STEMI protocols.

results.content: For ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), primary percutaneous coronary intervention within 90 minutes of first medical contact is preferred over fibrinolysis. Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor) is recommended for all acute coronary syndrome patients regardless of reperfusion strategy.
results.citation: Management of Acute Coronary Syndromes, ACC/AHA, 2025
